newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: BOXING - Boxer's folly costs dearly.
newsitem.headline: BOXING - Boxer's folly costs dearly.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Nov 21 - New Zealand light heavyweight boxer Regan Foley paid dearly for his folly in chasing to deck his opponent in South Africa on Thursday, NZPA reports.
He was knocked out himself as New Zealand's loss record in the All World Commonwealth Boxing tournament in Johannesburg stretched to four from four.
Foley led his bout by four points on all the judges' cards going into the third and final round, but then walked into his Irish opponent Stephen Kirk's punch.
"He fought very well, he was well ahead and then he went into the final round and started looking for the knockout punch," New Zealand trainer Chris Kenny said of Wanganui's Foley.
"In doing that he opened himself up and the Irishman put him away instead."
Foley's demise marked another unhappy night for New Zealand with bantamweight Noah Lopez outclassed by his Namibian opponent Albert Mutato.
"Noah was out-boxed, he was just not up to what was expected of him against his opponent," Kenny said.
"Basically, what this meet has shown us is that we need to take a far more professional attitude in our boxing.

"Virtually all the teams here in Johannesburg have been in camp for at least two weeks. We didn't do that. We picked our team after the nationals last month and then came over on a rushed arrangement.
"I think there is a lesson we have learned here that in future we need to be better prepared to match it with these guys."
Kenny said the New Zealand boxers also appeared to suffer from a lack of conditioning and were running out steam in the final round.
"They box all right for two rounds but then they run out of puff in the final round and that has shown up here," Kenny said.

With four of five New Zealand boxers, others being heavyweight Angus Shelford, of Auckland, and light heavyweight Tony DeVorms, of Tokoroa, losing in their first match, only super heavyweight Fai Falamoe is left to make his appearance at the tournament.
Falamoe's bout is on Saturday, New Zealand time.
"It's left to him now to fly the flag, we're hoping he goes well," Kenny said.
